[IARC.7.14] **libds carries its own `fma` on every row.** The fused
multiply-add [LEXP.3.2.2] requires must be one correctly rounded
implementation compiled into libds: musl's `fma`, from one pinned
release, compiled unmodified with the flags its pin records and
renamed, with every reference to it in libds's and CORE-MATH's objects, to a
name private to libds. A fused multiply-add CORE-MATH's functions compute
([IARC.7.10]) must be either that function or, on a row whose baseline ISA has
one, the fused multiply-add instruction. libds's objects must not reference
the C library's `fma`. This holds on every release row, with a hardware double
FPU or without one.

The C library's `fma` is the integrator's, and not every one rounds once: on
a row without a hardware fused multiply-add instruction in its baseline ISA,
calling it would make a `Float` result depend on the libc the integrator links.
The instruction and the private function compute the one value IEEE 754
defines for the operation, so which of them CORE-MATH executes moves no
result. The Mercury runtime's `math.fma` must call the same compiled function,
so both runtimes compute one value ([LDET.3.3a.8]). A change to the pin or the
flags admits each release row again before it ships ([NDET.1.4]).
